subject: general
question: By selling an article for ₹112, a man loses 25%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell it to gain 50%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Selling Prices: **SP₁ : SP₂ = (100 − Loss%) : (100 + Gain%)**

SP₁ : SP₂ = (100 − 25) : (100 + 50) = 75 : 150 = **1 : 2**

Given, 1 unit (SP₁) = **₹112**

Required Selling Price (SP₂) = 2 units = 112 × 2 = **₹224**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹224.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First Selling Price (SP₁) = **₹112**, Loss = **25%**, Target Gain = **50%**.
**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cba7168bc369fd87ebd5312492fa53fc08034f03c2c293092ce9fc2e0ad2479.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Cost Price (CP)**: CP = 112 × 100 ÷ (100 − 25)
⇒ CP = 112 × 100 ÷ 75 = 112 × 4 ÷ 3 = **₹448/3**
⇒ Calculate **New Selling Price (SP₂)**: SP₂ = (448/3) × (100 + 50) ÷ 100
⇒ SP₂ = (448/3) × 150 ÷ 100 = 448 × 50 ÷ 100 = 448 ÷ 2
⇒ SP₂ = **₹224**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹224.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base of CP

In profit and loss problems, **Cost Price (CP)** is always considered **100%** unless stated otherwise. Loss is subtracted from 100% and Profit is added to 100% to find SP%.

Unitary Method Application

If 75% (100 − 25) corresponds to ₹112, then 150% (100 + 50) will correspond to (112 ÷ 75) × 150.
